subject: Private Offer: buyer tiering & auto-approval rules for GridScale
messages:
From: John Davenport <john.davenport@gridscale.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer question — buyer approvals & terming

Diego,

Thanks for taking this — GridScale is evaluating Redwood for a consolidated inference offering across three internal business units. Procurement asked a few specific things we wanted to clarify before we proceed to legal:

- Can AWS private offers be configured so low-value buyers auto-approve (no manual buyer action) while high-value purchases require explicit procurement approval?
- Our org has mixed invoicing needs: one BU prefers annual invoices, others want monthly. Does a single private offer SKU support multiple billing cadences or do we need separate SKUs per BU?
- We're leaning toward a 6–9 month initial term with renewal options; any recommended seller-side term language that helps us avoid lengthy contract redlines?

Target timeline is ~2 weeks to get commercial terms into our procurement system. Any quick guidance or a template would be hugely helpful.

Appreciate it,
John Davenport
Head of Platform Partnerships
GridScale

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: John Davenport <john.davenport@gridscale.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer question — buyer approvals & terming

John — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below:

- Yes, we can gate by buyer thresholds (buyer-tiering) and configure auto-approval for low-dollar purchases. AWS Marketplace supports private offer buyer lists and custom approval flows, but seller-side config + marketplace ops coordination are needed.
- Multiple billing cadences often require separate SKUs or an SOW/invoice overlay; we typically recommend one SKU with a master SOW that defines invoicing cadence per BU to avoid SKU proliferation, unless your procurement insists on distinct purchase lines.
- For terms: a 6-month initial term with automatic renewals (30-day cancellation) typically reduces redlines; we include a clear billing start clause tied to first-production usage to address delay concerns.

I attached a short term-options summary to this message — see PO_Term_Options.pdf. Vanessa, Marcus: can you confirm the current auto-approval threshold matrix and whether we can implement a "buyer auto-approve under $X" rule in AWS private offers without requiring separate SKUs?

If it helps, we can run a quick procurement-ready template and open a co-sell enablement ticket with AWS marketplace ops. Do you want a one-pager for your procurement team or a full draft SOW?

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Sales Engineer, Marketplace
Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Private offer question — buyer approvals & terming

Folks — adding some operational detail from our marketplace playbook. Attachment: marketplace_auto_approval_matrix.xlsx (internal ops matrix). Key points: 

- Buyer tiering: we classify buyers into three bands by expected annualized spend for approval routing: Tier 1 (< $50k), Tier 2 ($50k–$250k), Tier 3 (> $250k).
  - Tier 1: can be configured for auto-approval in AWS private offers (no manual buyer procurement action). Works well for pilot BUs and developer teams.
  - Tier 2: requires a single procurement sign-off (purchase order upload or one-click from buyer). For multi-account buyers, AWS allows white-listing of account IDs on the private offer.
  - Tier 3: requires explicit legal & finance review, and we treat these as an escalation.

- Single SKU vs multiple SKUs: technically you can set a single SKU for a product and then include invoicing details in your SOW. If GridScale needs separate invoice lines for each BU in their ERP, separate SKUs simplify downstream accounting. Otherwise, prefer single SKU + SOW overlay (easier for rollouts).

- Auto-approval implementation: AWS Marketplace supports buyer lists and entitlement rules. We can set the private offer such that purchases from authorized account IDs under the Tier 1 threshold are auto-approved. There is an internal ops step to request that behavior from AWS marketplace ops; turnaround is typically 1–3 business days for configuration.

- Term recommendations: 6-month initial term with two automatic 6-month renewals (opt-out with 30 days' notice) tends to avoid buyer pushback. Add a "billing-start" clause: billing begins on first production usage or X days after signing, whichever comes first.

Next steps for us: I can prepare the config request to AWS (I need the list of account IDs you want whitelisted and a proposed auto-approve threshold). Diego: I'll own the ops ticket once we have the account IDs + threshold.

-Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Marketplace Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa & team — helpful. A few clarifications from procurement's side: 

- GridScale would prefer a 6-month initial term with option to renew annually after the pilot period; procurement said they can accept an initial 6-month commitment but prefer invoices on an annual cadence for budgeting reasons. Would Redwood be open to annual invoicing for a 6-month initial term?
- For the auto-approve threshold: we want auto-approval for up to $50k per account per 30-day period (this covers most pilot usage). Anything above that should trigger the Tier 2 flow.
- Account scoping: we have 7 AWS account IDs spread across three org units. Procurement prefers a single PO line that covers all accounts if possible. If not, they asked how much overhead separate SKUs would add on Redwood/AWS side.

We need to close the commercial terms in the next 10 business days to make our Q2 budget cycle. Diego — can you propose the exact wording for the billing and auto-approval clauses so we can circulate internally? Also happy to hop on a 30-minute call to finalize.

Regards,

John — thanks, and appreciate the timeline. Below is proposed commercial language you can drop into procurement review, plus next steps.

Proposed clauses (for procurement):
1) Term & Renewal: Initial term of six (6) months commencing on the later of (a) the Effective Date or (b) the date of first production usage. Following the Initial Term, the Agreement shall automatically renew for successive one (1) year terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days prior to the then-current term's expiration.

2) Billing: Seller shall invoice Buyer annually in arrears unless Buyer requests alternate invoicing cadence. For the Initial Term only, Seller will accept annual invoicing with a 6-month commitment represented on Redwood's invoice. Invoices may reference underlying account-level usage; rights to invoice consolidation to a single buyer entity will be honored where feasible.

3) Buyer auto-approval & account scoping: Seller will configure the AWS Private Offer to whitelist the Buyer-provided AWS account IDs. Purchases by whitelisted accounts that are under Fifty Thousand Dollars (USD $50,000) per thirty (30) day period shall be auto-approved and processed without additional manual procurement action. Purchases exceeding that threshold shall be routed to Tier 2 procurement approval. Seller reserves the right to escalate any Tier 3 purchases (>$250,000) to legal/finance review prior to fulfillment.

4) SKU & SOW: One (1) SKU will be provisioned for the product; Buyer and Seller shall enter into a separate Statement of Work (SOW) that documents account-level invoicing preferences and any special billing instructions. If Buyer requires discrete invoicing lines per AWS account for ERP purposes, separate SKUs will be recommended and may be created upon mutual agreement.

Next steps:
- John: send the list of the seven AWS account IDs you want whitelisted and confirm you accept the $50k/30-day auto-approval threshold.
- Vanessa: please open the AWS ops configuration ticket once we have the account IDs (assign to marketplace-ops).
- Marcus: I'll drop a draft SOW (draft_sow.docx) into the HubSpot deal and share DocuSign link for procurement to review the billing clause.

I'll also schedule a 30-minute call for Tues 27 Apr to walk procurement through the language unless you prefer a different time.

Best,
